title: The notebook copilot: evidence-backed review notes beside every cell
request: An intelligent assistant that corrects data scientists where they work: a comment or suggestion beside every notebook cell, each with tested evidence ('show the proof'), like finding on Stack Overflow that someone already hit and solved the problem.
spec: dclab_rnd/copilot/: a static, order-aware review of a notebook (never executes code) whose findings each carry a concrete fix, the DCLab rules they violate and a measured precedent from the campaigns; Markdown, annotated-notebook and HTML views; leaky and clean demo notebooks. Beside it, the local notebook companion (dclab_rnd/notebook_assist.py) with cell-level advice in an output contract a VS Code extension can read.
plan: Parse each cell's code and walk the notebook in order, carrying what was split, fitted and selected across cells.
Detect the measured pitfalls (fit or selection before the split or CV, oversampling, target encoding, blocked columns, random splits on dated data, holdout reuse, missing seeds).
Attach curated rule ids and a precedent retrieved from the evidence index with type and dataset filters.
Render the review three ways and build a leaky and a clean demo notebook.
Run it on the owner's part1 HyperAck notebook.
Merge the owner's local notebook-assistant work into the reorganized layout.

decisions.decision: Review statically; never execute the notebook.
decisions.why: Reviewing must be safe on any notebook, including ones with side effects or private data paths.

decisions.decision: Attach curated rule ids, not fuzzy matches, and a measured precedent as proof.
decisions.why: A data scientist should be able to check the claim against a number DCLab measured.

decisions.decision: Leave the owner's lower-severity notebook issues for the owner.
decisions.why: Only the leak was asked to be fixed; scaling before the split, a random split on dated rows and an absolute file path were reported, not changed.

change: dclab_rnd/copilot/ (analyzer, fixes, render, CLI), demo notebooks, docs/guides/NOTEBOOK_COPILOT.md; then the companion (notebook_assist.py, notebook_assist_eval.py, notebook_eval.py) from pull request 1, fitted into the new layout; and the leak fix in the part1 HyperAck notebook.

findings.defect: The owner's part1 HyperAck notebook trained on the two post-outcome final fares.
findings.scenario: The copilot flagged that preprocess_data kept final_customer_fare and final_biker_fare as model inputs, though both are only known after the order outcome; the saved models in that notebook's folder were trained with them.
findings.cause: The exploratory notebook predates the safe-vs-unsafe analysis and never dropped the fares.
findings.fix: Drop both columns in preprocess_data with a comment explaining why; the saved models stay wrong until the notebook is rerun.
findings.test: Re-reviewing the notebook reports no high-severity finding.

findings.defect: The merged notebook-assistant work broke the suite.
findings.scenario: Pull request 1 used pre-reorganization paths: seven tests failed, and three test modules imported code that was never pushed (replay_compare, system_eval, trace_eval).
findings.cause: The work was written against the old layout on another machine.
findings.fix: Move the prototype folder under research/agentic-ml-copilot/, read evidence from its new place, map notebook paths recorded before the reorganization through a resolver so a frozen manifest still works, and make tests that need files only on the author's machine skip with a message naming the missing file.
findings.test: The suite passes; the skipped tests run as soon as the missing files are committed.

measurements.name: demo notebooks
measurements.gate: The leaky demo must draw high-severity notes and the careful version none.
measurements.result: The leaky demo reports accuracy 96.7% and gets three high-severity notes; the careful version of the same analysis gets no notes and an honest ROC-AUC of 0.804.
measurements.next: Measure precision on real notebooks labelled by reviewers (AGT-003), not on demos.

outcome: A working copilot with proof links and a companion contract for VS Code; it found and fixed a real leak in the owner's own notebook. Its accuracy on real, unseen notebooks is not yet measured.
lessons: Point a new reviewer at your own work first; the copilot's first real finding was in the owner's notebook.
Code merged from another machine must be checked against the current layout before it lands.
